title: Install Ops Sprint Echo - Weekly Briefing
content:
Sprint Echo — Private Deployments weekly briefing (notes + live action items)

Period: 2028-03-05 to 2028-03-07 (standup cadence: M/W/F)
Owner: Priya Anand (install ops lead)
Attendees: Marcus Lee, Sofia Hernandez, Aaron Kim, Leah O'Connor, field eng oncall (Ravi), solutions SE (Nadia)

TL;DR
- Two customer installs in active canary. Both progressing but each has a persistent, distinct blocker: one is a VXLAN MTU mismatch against customer firewall (in-flight packet drops); other is NVMe firmware skew causing docker layer corruption during heavy snapshotting. No customer-facing downtime; degraded performance observed in canary (p95 tokens +70ms).
- KMS rotation plan for private-control plane delayed by policy question from legal; holding off until we get sign-off on envelope wrapping (JIRA PD-7124).
- Networking playbook gaps identified for cross-VPC routing — action to augment runbook with a short checklist and expected iptables/calico checks.

Detailed notes
1) Canary: Acadia Corp (VPC, reserved capacity) — progress
   - Work done: base install complete, model artifacts loaded, certs provisioned via customer KMS (test key).
   - Observation: intermittent packet fragmentation from worker nodes to external customer DB proxy. Root cause hypothesis: VXLAN MTU default (1400) < customer transit MTU (1500) + firewall path causing fragments dropped by stateful firewall when fragments lack port info.
   - Evidence: tcpdump (on node) shows frequent IP fragments and DF=0 on large token responses. Cloud vendor SR shows firewall logging 'fragmentation needed' for several flows.
   - Mitigation attempted: lowered max_response_chunk to 1024 tokens to reduce UDP-like large responses; temporary path MTU discovery toggled. Partial improvement, p95 latency still +45ms.
   - Action items: 
     * Marcus: schedule with customer net-eng to align MTU and validate firewall fragmentation rules. Due: 2028-03-09. Linked: NET-1987.
     * Aaron: add quick-check script to install checklist that verifies MTU/pmtu along the route and validates that DF=1 flows succeed for a 1500-byte payload. Due: 2028-03-08.

2) Canary: Borealis (On-prem rack install) — NVMe firmware skew
   - Symptom: under heavy snapshotting the node's container filesystem reported checksums mismatch and overlayfs errors; triggers container restarts and model warmth loss.
   - Root cause: mixed NVMe firmware versions across the RAID causing a known vendor bug under heavy parallel IO (vendor KB 4.7.2). Not a Redwood runtime bug but surfaced during our heavy snapshot scenario.
   - Workaround: throttle snapshot concurrency (config change), set iostats-based backoff in snapshotter, and pin to single-threaded fsync for critical snapshots.
   - Permanent fix plan: vendor has a firmware roll-forward; on-site ops scheduled firmware update (maintenance window) + validation test harness.
   - Action items:
     * Leah: coordinate on-site maintenance window with customer (preferred weekend). Due: 2028-03-10.
     * Field eng (Ravi): prepare pre/post health check script (nvme smart, fio snapshot sim) and drop into runbook. Due: 2028-03-09.

3) KMS envelope rotation — blocked by legal policy question
   - Description: we planned a rolling KMS key rotation for private-control plane (affects customer-managed KMS integrations). Legal flagged an ambiguity in our envelope-wrapping doc: whether we log key IDs in telemetry (we currently do not). Need explicit acceptance for the rotation flow before proceeding with onprem customer schedule.
   - Action items:
     * Priya: draft succinct note for Legal and Security summarizing telemetry minimalism and commit to an opt-in audit log flag. Due: 2028-03-07.
     * Nadia (solutions SE): prepare customer-facing FAQ for KMS rotation steps and rollback. Due: 2028-03-12.

4) Observability: Canary metrics and anomalies
   - Canary baseline: host CPU steal spiked on Acadia nodes during heavy token generation bursts — correlate with host-level backup jobs overlapping.
   - Traces: sampling shows token generation tailing in runtime queue ~120ms during spikes.
   - Small win: enabling transparent prefix caching for identical prompt pairs on canary reduced token generation by 18% for repeated tests. Consider enabling in next canary stage.
   - Action items:
     * Marcus: add guard to schedule backups outside peak inference windows in the install guide. Due: 2028-03-09.
     * SRE: validate and recommend default caching TTL for canaries. (SRE ticket: SRE-3012).

5) Runbook gaps and quick wins
   - Found: troubleshooting matrix lacks a simple first-steps checklist for 'partial connectivity' vs 'fragmentation' vs 'BGP path MTU'. This causes field eng to run long diagnostics.
   - Quick wins: add a 2-min checklist (icmp pmtu, traceroute -F, iptables conntrack inspect) and preserve sample tcpdump command we used.
   - Action item: Aaron to author runbook appendix and check-in PR to private-deploy runbook repo. Due: 2028-03-11.

6) Customer escalations and handoffs
   - Acadia asked for an SLA note: what to expect if fragmentation persists after MTU align. We proposed staged mitigation (reduce chunk size -> enable reassembly proxy -> temporary TLS tunneling). Customer requested cost estimate for tunnel option.
   - Borealis requested evidence package for vendor firmware issue to accelerate hardware vendor support. We provided logs and fio traces; vendor wants full NVMe dumps.
   - Action items:
     * Priya: assemble cost/ops note for tunnel option and share with Sales (cc: Nadia). Due: 2028-03-10.
     * Leah: collect NVMe dumps and coordinate access to vendor portal. Due: 2028-03-08.

7) Risks + blockers (summary)
   - Legal KMS question blocks rotation schedule for multiple customers (medium severity).
   - Network fragmentation risk remains until customer firewall MTU alignment — could cause degraded p95s in canary (low -> medium risk to SLA depending on customer tolerance).
   - Hardware firmware roll required for onprem customer; scheduling and vendor lead time uncertain (medium risk).

8) Dependencies and cross-team asks
   - Legal & Security: quick review of KMS envelope note. (PD-7124)
   - SRE: help confirm backup scheduling guidance and caching TTL defaults. (SRE-3012)
   - Solutions/Sales: estimate cost for temporary TLS tunnel option for Acadia.

Open questions (need quick answers)
- Should we add a binary toggle in the install script to reduce response chunk size for customers behind restrictive firewalls, or treat as manual mitigation? (input from product)
- For NVMe firmware: can vendor supply signed firmware image to preload into our deployment packaging for faster fix? (vendor auth question)

Meeting cadence and next steps
- Next focused network troubleshooting session: 2028-03-08 09:00 PT (Marcus, customer net-eng, Priya).
- Runbook PR to be published by 2028-03-11 (Aaron).
- KMS legal note expected 2028-03-07; if no blocker, start scheduling rotations week of 2028-03-20.

Appendix (raw snippets)
- tcpdump sample command used: sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/acadia-frags.pcap host 10.12.4.5 and not port 22
- quick fio profile used for NVMe repro: fio --name=nvme-burst --ioengine=libaio --rw=randrw --bs=4k --numjobs=8 --iodepth=64 --runtime=600
- minimal MTU check: ip route get 8.8.8.8; tracepath -n <dest>

Notes-to-self (choppy)
- follow up on PD-7124 legal q — escalate if no reply by EOD 3/7
- remind SRE re: caching defaults — mention canary metric drop
- vault access token refresh with onprem ops (Leah)

If anything urgent surfaces outside cadence ping: #private-deployments-install on Slack and escalate to oncall (Ravi).

-- Priya
